audiences.title: Built for the teams that control and use the repertoire

label.label: Labels & label groups
label.question: Can our repertoire, current and back catalogue, be surfaced from the references that matter now?
label.route: Private Catalogue Pilot: test on a representative authorised sample first.
label.conversation: Catalogue scope, reference tracks, reviewers and an agreed scorecard.

dist.label: Distributors
dist.question: Can we make thousands of distributed releases discoverable beyond text metadata?
dist.route: Pilot first, then API + managed ingestion for catalogue-scale onboarding.
dist.conversation: Catalogue breadth, ingestion cadence and metadata quality.

store.label: Stores & platforms
store.question: Can sound-first discovery deepen the user journey without replacing our storefront?
store.route: API + Catalogue Ingestion: your interface, your customer relationship.
store.conversation: Integration surface, service mode and the evaluation route.

cat.label: Catalogue teams
cat.question: Which assets are hard to find, inconsistently described, or worth a campaign?
cat.route: Private Catalogue Pilot, with metadata review included in scope.
cat.conversation: Sample composition, review workflow and evidence needs.

tech.label: Music technology products
tech.question: Can we add similarity and track analysis without building the signal-processing layer?
tech.route: API first: scoped key against an indexed evaluation catalogue.
tech.conversation: Endpoints, response structures and integration planning.

control.title: Your catalogue stays yours
statements: You retain catalogue ownership and commercial control.
Partner catalogues are logically isolated and restricted to authorised partner access.
Similarity searches only the catalogue authorised for that partner.
PYXIS-1 does not train or fine-tune itself on partner audio, and does not generate derivative audio.
No public sandbox or shared partner catalogue exists.
Detailed rights, retention and deletion terms are agreed for the relevant service.
